title: Short Stuff: Safety Pins
summary: Short Stuff episode on the safety pin and its inventor Walter Hunt. The hosts open with light banter about amusement park height requirements and roller coasters, then cover Hunt's 1849 safety pin, which they say is virtually identical to modern versions, and the legend that he made it to pay off a fifteen dollar debt and sold the patent for about twelve thousand dollars (they mention a four hundred dollar figure as well). They then discuss Hunt's earlier sewing machine invention, which he reportedly did not patent because his daughter pointed out it would put seamstresses out of work, and the later Elias Howe and Isaac Singer patent dispute, in which a judge ruled Hunt was the inventor but too late to file a patent retroactively. They note other Hunt inventions, the punk fashion use of safety pins with the disputed origin (Richard Hell versus Johnny Rotten), and close with the website and contact info.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Short Stuff

segments.title: Opening banter on height requirements and roller coasters
segments.summary: The hosts joke about amusement park height limits and childhood fears of roller coasters, including Space Mountain experiences.

segments.title: Walter Hunt and the 1849 safety pin
segments.summary: Walter Hunt, a nineteenth century American inventor, invented the safety pin in 1849; the hosts say its design is virtually the same as modern safety pins. The legend says he made it to settle a fifteen dollar debt and sold the patent for a sum they describe as about twelve thousand dollars, after mentioning a four hundred dollar figure.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief break before returning to the sewing machine story.

segments.title: Walter Hunt's sewing machine and the Howe-Singer patent fight
segments.summary: Hunt reportedly invented an early sewing machine decades before others, with a curved eye needle and shuttle, but did not patent it, reportedly because his daughter noted it would put seamstresses out of work. The hosts say his prototype was wooden. Elias Howe held the patent, and Isaac Singer built machines on the same design; in court a judge ruled Hunt was the true inventor but too late to file retroactively.

segments.title: Other Hunt inventions and movie pitch joke
segments.summary: The hosts mention other Hunt inventions, including a foot pedal alarm for street cars and an antipodean walking device (suction cup shoes). They joke about a movie about the inventor and possible titles.

segments.title: Safety pins in punk fashion
segments.summary: Safety pins became a punk fashion accessory in the 1970s. Richard Hell is credited by some with the idea, while Johnny Rotten of the Sex Pistols reportedly said they were used to hold up trousers. The hosts joke about Hunt's ghost disapproving of face piercings.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up and direct listeners to the website and email address for contact.
